_comment: Sprint 35 curated fishing-guidance catalogue: common surf/pier targets only, region-gated by conditions_region. Every field except id/name/regions is copied verbatim from the legacy storage/species_data.json entry named in legacy_name (provisional dataset, see docs/CANONICAL_ROADMAP.md). Generated by scripts/generate_guidance_catalogue.py; regenerate rather than hand-edit.

species.name: Red drum
species.bait: Cut menhaden or mullet strips; fresh shrimp; live finger mullet when available
species.rig: Fish finder rig with sliding egg sinker
species.lures: Gold/copper spoons, paddle-tail swimbaits (3-5"), Z-Man soft plastics on 1/4-3/8 oz jighead, topwater plugs at dawn/dusk
species.explanation_cold: Winter red drum congregate in deeper marsh channels and holes, foraging along the bottom for shrimp, crabs and small fish.
species.explanation_warm: Red drum actively feed in the surf zone and around inlets, chasing mullet, menhaden and crabs in warmer water.

species.name: Black drum
species.bait: Cut shrimp, clams, blood worms, cut mullet, menhaden or crab pieces
species.rig: Hi-lo rig or fish finder rig
species.lures: Not a primary lure target; slow-rolled paddle-tail swimbaits near oyster structure occasionally work
species.explanation_cold: Black drum are bottom feeders that locate prey with chin barbels; they prefer mollusks, shrimp and crab pieces in cooler water.
species.explanation_warm: Black drum move through inlets and along structure, actively rooting for crabs, clams and shrimp in warming water.

species.name: Bluefish
species.bait: Cut menhaden or mullet; small fish pieces
species.rig: Fish finder rig with steel leader
species.lures: Metal spoons (Hopkins, Kastmaster), topwater poppers, Clarkspoons, metal jigs; bluefish hit almost any fast-moving lure
species.explanation_cold: Smaller bluefish (snappers/tailors) roam nearshore waters and readily hit cut bait; wire or heavy leaders are essential.
species.explanation_warm: Bluefish schools are actively chasing baitfish along the surf line and around piers; cut menhaden and mullet draw explosive strikes.

species.name: Speckled trout
species.bait: Live shrimp (most productive); finger mullet; small menhaden
species.rig: Popping-cork or fishfinder rig on light leader
species.lures: MirrOlure (MR17, 52M), soft plastic tails (Gulp shrimp, DOA Terror Eyz) on 1/4 oz jighead, topwater walk-the-dog lures
species.explanation_cold: Speckled trout hold in deeper holes and backwater creeks; live shrimp or finger mullet entice sluggish winter fish.
species.explanation_warm: Speckled trout are aggressively feeding on shrimp and small baitfish in the shallows and around grass flats.

species.name: Whiting (sea mullet)
species.bait: Fresh shrimp, mole crabs (sand fleas), bloodworms, squid
species.rig: Hi-lo rig with small hooks
species.lures: Small jigs (1/16-1/8 oz) tipped with Fishbites; not a primary lure target
species.explanation_cold: Whiting patrol sandy bottoms along beaches and piers; they feed on shrimp, mole crabs and worms in the winter surf.
species.explanation_warm: Whiting are schooling up along the beach and biting aggressively on shrimp and sand fleas in the wash zone.

species.name: Spot
species.bait: Bloodworms; small pieces of shrimp; Fishbites
species.rig: Hi-lo rig with small hooks
species.lures: Rarely taken on lures; not a primary lure target
species.explanation_cold: Spot are mostly offshore or in deeper channels during winter; occasional catches from piers on warmer days.
species.explanation_warm: Spot are schooling along the beach and around piers, biting aggressively on bloodworms and shrimp pieces.

species.name: Atlantic croaker
species.bait: Fresh shrimp pieces; bloodworms; squid strips; Fishbites
species.rig: Hi-lo rig with small hooks
species.lures: Not typically lure-caught; small jigs occasionally work
species.explanation_cold: Croaker move to deeper channels and offshore in winter; occasional catches from piers on mild days.
species.explanation_warm: Croaker are schooling along the surf and around piers, making their signature croaking sound; they hit shrimp and worms aggressively.

species.name: Sheepshead
species.bait: Live fiddler crabs; sand fleas; small pieces of shrimp
species.rig: Knocker rig with short fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Rarely taken on lures; small jigs with soft crab imitations near pilings occasionally work
species.explanation_cold: Sheepshead feed around pilings and rock structures, nibbling barnacles and crustaceans; bites are subtle and require fishing straight down.
species.explanation_warm: Sheepshead stack up around nearshore structure and pilings, picking at barnacles and crabs before moving offshore for spawning.

species.name: Flounder
species.bait: Live finger mullet; live minnows; fresh shrimp under a bucktail jig
species.rig: Fish finder rig with 24-36 in fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Bucktail jig (1/4-1/2 oz) with paddle tail, Gulp Nemesis or shrimp, Carolina-rigged swimming grub bounced on bottom
species.explanation_cold: Flounder are mostly offshore in cold water; stragglers around inlets may bite live mullet drifted slowly along the bottom.
species.explanation_warm: Flounder are ambushing baitfish in the surf, around inlets and near pier pilings; live finger mullet is the top producer.

species.name: Pompano
species.bait: Sand fleas (mole crabs); fresh shrimp; Fishbites
species.rig: Pompano rig with float beads above hooks
species.lures: Pompano jigs (1/4-3/8 oz, yellow/orange/chartreuse), Silly Willy jigs, Clouser minnows near breaking waves
species.explanation_cold: Pompano are scarce inshore during cold months; occasional catches occur on warmer days near the surf zone.
species.explanation_warm: Pompano are running the surf line feeding on sand fleas and small crustaceans; target the troughs and holes along the beach.

species.name: Spanish mackerel
species.bait: Shiny spoons; live baitfish; small plugs; fresh shrimp on a long-shank hook
species.rig: Float rig with wire leader, free-lined or under float
species.lures: Clarkspoon (1/0-3/0) on inline spinner or planer, small metal jigs, silver or gold spoons; fast retrieve
species.explanation_cold: Spanish mackerel have migrated south; they are not present in nearshore NC waters during cold months.
species.explanation_warm: Spanish mackerel are blitzing baitfish just behind the breakers and around piers; they hit flashy spoons and small baits.

species.name: Snook
species.bait: Live mullet; live shrimp; live menhaden; topwater plugs
species.rig: Fish finder rig with heavy fluorocarbon leader or free-lined
species.lures: Large soft plastic jerkbaits, DOA Baitbuster, topwater walk-the-dog plugs, Rapala X-Rap; target structure and inlet edges
species.explanation_cold: Snook are a tropical species not found in NC during cold months.
species.explanation_warm: Snook are rare visitors to NC during unusually warm summers; they are prized gamefish that ambush bait around inlets, docks and structure.

species.name: Striped bass
species.bait: Cut menhaden, mullet or shad; live mullet or eels
species.rig: Fish finder rig with heavy fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Bucktail jigs (1-3 oz), soft plastic swimbaits, topwater plugs (Rapala X-Rap, Bomber), metal jigs at night under lights
species.explanation_cold: Striped bass are found around piers, jetties and surf troughs; winter surf anglers use cut or live bait on heavy tackle.
species.explanation_warm: Striped bass push through inlets chasing schools of mullet and menhaden; they are most active at dawn and dusk.

species.name: Tautog
species.bait: Pieces of fresh shrimp, sand fleas, fiddler or rock crabs, clams
species.rig: Knocker rig with heavy fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Not a strong lure target; slow-rolled swimbaits near rocky structure occasionally work
species.explanation_cold: Tautog cling to jetties and rock piles in winter, feeding on crustaceans; they require strong tackle and small, strong hooks.
species.explanation_warm: Tautog become less active as water warms and move to deeper structure; early spring offers a window before they thin out.

species.name: Black sea bass
species.bait: Strips of squid or cut fish; shrimp
species.rig: Hi-lo rig on braided line
species.lures: Small jigs (1-2 oz bucktail), soft plastic crabs/shrimp on drop-shot rigs, small diamond jigs near structure
species.explanation_cold: Inshore black sea bass inhabit wrecks and hard bottom, feeding on crabs, shrimp and small fish; bottom-fish with squid or cut bait.
species.explanation_warm: Black sea bass are abundant over nearshore reefs and wrecks, aggressively hitting squid strips and cut bait.

species.name: Barred surfperch
species.bait: Sand crabs (mole crabs); bloodworms; Gulp! sandworms; small pieces of mussel
species.rig: Carolina rig with light leader; sliding sinker rig
species.lures: Small paddle-tail swimbaits (2-3"), Berkley Gulp Sand Crab, tube jigs in the surf zone
species.explanation_cold: Barred surfperch are actively spawning and feeding aggressively in the winter surf zone -- this is peak season on the Pacific Coast.
species.explanation_warm: Barred surfperch are present but less concentrated; they move to deeper water as surf warms.

species.name: Redtail surfperch
species.bait: Sand crabs; sand shrimp; pile worms; Gulp! sandworms
species.rig: Carolina rig or double dropper loop rig
species.lures: Small paddle tails, Gulp Sand Crab in the surf; same tactics as barred surfperch
species.explanation_cold: Redtail surfperch school up in the surf zone during winter and early spring, feeding heavily on sand crabs in the wash.
species.explanation_warm: Redtail surfperch are less common in the surf during warmer months; try rocky areas and jetties.

species.name: California halibut
species.bait: Live anchovy; live smelt; squid strips; Gulp! grubs; swim baits
species.rig: Sliding sinker rig with fluorocarbon leader; Carolina rig; jig head
species.sinker: 1-3 oz sliding egg or banana sinker
species.lures: Live bait-style swimbaits, paddle tails on 3/8-3/4 oz jighead, Berkley Gulp grubs drifted on bottom
species.explanation_cold: California halibut are in deeper water during cold months and less accessible from shore.
species.explanation_warm: California halibut move into shallow sandy areas near piers, jetties, and in the surf zone to ambush baitfish; cast parallel to shore and retrieve slowly along the bottom.

species.name: Corbina
species.bait: Sand crabs; bloodworms; mussels; clam
species.rig: Carolina rig with light fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Berkley Gulp Sand Crab, small swimbaits, Yamamoto Senko-style worms in the surf
species.explanation_cold: Corbina move to deeper water and are hard to reach from shore in winter.
species.explanation_warm: Corbina cruise the SoCal surf zone rooting for sand crabs and worms in the wash; they are the prized surf species of Southern California.

species.name: Yellowfin croaker
species.bait: Sand crabs; mussels; bloodworms; cut squid
species.rig: Carolina rig; sliding sinker rig
species.lures: Small swimbaits, Gulp lures
species.explanation_cold: Yellowfin croaker are deeper and less active during cold months.
species.explanation_warm: Yellowfin croaker are common in the SoCal and central CA surf zone; they school up and feed aggressively on sand crabs.

species.name: Black rockfish
species.bait: Live or cut herring; tube worms; squid strips; live anchovies
species.rig: Light to medium tackle; drift-fishing with a single hook on 20-30 lb leader; jig straight down to schools
species.lures: Tube jigs in black/purple, soft plastic paddle tails, metal jigs (Crippled Herring), and Buzz Bombs — black rockfish readily hit surface lures
species.explanation_cold: Black rockfish hold near rocky reefs and kelp at 30-150 ft year-round; they are less active in winter but can be found schooling tight to structure.
species.explanation_warm: Spring and summer are prime for black rockfish along the Pacific coast; they school near the surface around kelp beds and rocky points and aggressively hit surface poppers, tube jigs, and cut herring.

species.name: Lingcod
species.bait: Live bait (smelt, anchovy); large swimbaits; jigs tipped with squid
species.rig: Heavy jig head or dropper loop rig with large swimbait
species.lures: Large swimbaits (5-8"), heavy jigs (4-8 oz), plastic eels; very aggressive; retrieve with erratic action
species.explanation_cold: Lingcod move into shallower rocky reefs during fall and winter to spawn; they are aggressive ambush predators accessible from jetties and rocky points.
species.explanation_warm: Lingcod retreat to deeper water offshore during warm months; less accessible from shore.

species.name: Ulua (giant trevally)
species.bait: Live akule (bigeye scad); live opelu; large cut bait; whole octopus
species.rig: Heavy sliding sinker rig with 100+ lb leader; ulua setup
species.lures: Large poppers, stickbaits (GT poppers), heavy swimbaits; very powerful fighter
species.explanation_cold: Giant trevally are present year-round in Hawaii but slightly less active during cooler months.
species.explanation_warm: Giant trevally (ulua) are the ultimate shore-fishing trophy in Hawaii; they're powerful predators caught from rocky shores and piers on heavy tackle.

species.name: Papio
species.bait: Live opelu; cut squid; shrimp; small crabs; poppers
species.rig: Light papio rig; float rig; small sliding sinker
species.lures: Small jigs, spoons, swimbaits; juvenile jacks are aggressive
species.explanation_cold: Papio are present year-round in Hawaii; smaller jacks are always near shore.
species.explanation_warm: Papio are the most popular shore-fishing target in Hawaii; these juvenile jacks roam reefs and harbors and are a great family fishing species.

species.name: O'io (bonefish)
species.bait: Shrimp; sand crabs; small crabs; squid strips; fly fishing (Christmas Island specials)
species.rig: Light Carolina rig with fluorocarbon leader
species.lures: Clouser minnows, shrimp fly imitations, Crazy Charlie flies; almost exclusively sight-fished with lures/flies
species.explanation_cold: Bonefish are present year-round in Hawaii flats but slightly less active in winter.
species.explanation_warm: Bonefish (oio) feed on shallow sand flats in Hawaii; they are the ghosts of the flats -- fast, wary, and an incredible fight on light tackle.

species.name: Moi
species.bait: Sand crabs; shrimp; cut squid; small crabs
species.rig: Sliding sinker rig in the surf; Carolina rig with fluorocarbon
species.lures: Small jigs, soft plastics; delicate fighters
species.explanation_cold: Moi are present in cooler months but less concentrated in the shallows.
species.explanation_warm: Moi (Pacific threadfin) is Hawaii's most revered eating fish; once reserved for royalty, they feed in the sandy surf zone and are caught from beaches and piers.
